messages:
Anita G: Auditor asked for proof of RBAC change approvals and KMS key rotation events for the last 12 months. They also want vulnerability triage notes linked to any changes. Can we assemble artifacts by EOD?

Sara L: I'm on it. I'll gather PR approvals, JIRA change tickets, and the RBAC policy diffs. Where should we put the KMS rotation logs?

Mike P: Put exports in the secure S3 bucket: s3://redwood-audit-exports/{org}/. Use lifecycle to restrict public access. For AWS CloudTrail rotation events you can run:
```
aws cloudtrail lookup-events --lookup-attributes AttributeKey=EventName,AttributeValue=RotateKey --start-time 2023-03-01 --end-time 2024-03-01
```
This returns Console and CLI rotations; include KeyId filter.

Sara L: thanks. I'll run that and scrub ARNs for PII. Also will include periodic rotation policy doc link: https://redwood.internal/docs/kms/key-rotation

compliance-bot: Evidence export created: export-1732468019.tar.gz -> s3://redwood-audit-exports/2024-03/audit-package-1732468019

Jon R: For vuln triage, auditor wants the timeline and mitigation notes for any change that came from a finding. We should include the security triage issue (e.g., RED-4567) and the patch PR + verification logs.

Anita G: Also include emergency access logs (breakglass) and approval emails. Auditor specifically asked for who approved temporary role escalations during incidents.

Mike P: To pull breakglass events (assume AWS IAM for example):
```
aws cloudtrail lookup-events --lookup-attributes AttributeKey=EventName,AttributeValue=AssumeRole --start-time 2023-01-01 --end-time 2024-03-01 --query 'Events[?contains(CloudTrailEvent, `breakglass`)]'
```
We'll need to correlate with PagerDuty incident IDs.

Sara L: I'll assemble a manifest.csv with columns: artifact_name, artifact_type, created_by, created_at, source_link, redaction_status. Example row:
```
audit-manifest.csv
artifact-1, PR, sara.l@redwood.com, 2024-02-05, https://github.com/redwood/repo/pull/123, redacted
```

Sara L: Quick Q: Do we include raw CloudTrail JSON or a zipped, redacted subset? Auditors sometimes want raw but security prefers redacted. Thoughts?

Jon R: Provide raw to compliance team only, and a redacted copy for the auditor. Record the redaction method in the manifest.

Anita G: Agreed. @Mike P can you produce the raw export to the secure bucket and then a redacted copy we can hand off.

Mike P: Yup. I'll run exports, checksum them, and drop both. I'll add a SHA256_<filename>.sig file for integrity checks.

Sara L: Estimated ETA: raw export + manifest by 17:30 PT today. Then I'll create the auditor package and upload to the auditor portal.

Anita G: Perfect. When uploading, tag the package with control IDs: SOC2-CC6, ISO27001-A.12.1.3

Mike P: one more note — include the KMS key policy change PRs and KMS CMK tags. Sample log snippet I'll include in the bundle:
```
2024-02-05T16:12:03Z  RotateKey KeyId=arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:123456789012:key/abcd-ef01
2024-02-06T02:04:11Z  CreateGrant GrantId=xyz
```

Anita G: Thanks team. I'll follow up with the auditor after upload and ask for any missing items.

Sara L: uploading now to s3://redwood-audit-exports/2024-03/audit-package-1732468019.tar.gz :thumbsup: 

compliance-bot: Upload complete. Package size 124MB. Access granted to auditor@auditfirm.com until 2024-04-15.
